newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude corrects lower, gas oil little changed.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude corrects lower, gas oil little changed.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were sharply lower in early trade on Friday, as the market corrected back from Thursday's close, brokers said.
By 0945 GMT front month crude was 22 cents lower at $18.72 a barrel, while August gas oil was unchanged on the day at $169.25 a tonne.
"Thursday's close was bid up quite strongly," one broker said. "It was an aberration. We're just seeing a bit of a correction."
But brokers did not expect to see the downtrend continue in the long-term.
"I'm not convinced the market is in a collapse situation," said a broker, who pegged crude support at Thursday's lows of $18.50 a barrel.
News from the United Nations overnight that Iraq's aid distribution plan would get the go-ahead early next week was unlikely to have much impact on the market, brokers said.
But while brokers said the U.N. news was already factored-in and was unlikely to throw the market, the shorter term trend was seen by some to remain downwards.
"The UN news was already doing the rounds on Thursday afternoon," one broker said.
"But I don't see crude making fresh highs."
September Brent closed just three cents lower at $18.94 a barrel on Thursday after U.S. products expiries ruffled the market sending crude into a choppy 60 cent trading range.
Crude bounced back in late Thursday trade after the speculative dump of gasoline futures in New York ahead of unleaded gasoline August contract expiry.
A UN spokesman attributed the delay in the rubber stamping of Iraq's aid distribution plan to a computer virus affecting one of the diskettes containing Baghdad's proposals.
"It is settled from our point of view. We asked Iraq for certain assurances ... and we received them in writing," the spokesman said.
